Procs

proc csrf(options: CsrfOptions = defaultCsrfOptions()): AsyncMiddleware {.
    ...raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Double-submit CSRF token protection.

A token is issued as a cookie and echoed back by the client in the headerName header (default x-csrf-token) or the formField form field. Safe methods (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS by default) skip validation.

The default is a JS-readable cookie (httpOnlyCookie = false) because the header double-submit model needs the client to read the cookie. For plain-HTTP (non-TLS) deployments set allowInsecureCookie = true and secureCookie = false; otherwise the cookie is never sent over HTTP and validation always fails.

allowQueryToken accepts the token from the query string. Keep it disabled unless required: tokens in URLs leak through Referer headers, access logs, and browser history.

The form-field fallback reads "form_" & formField from req.locals, which the urlencoded body parser populates; register a body parser (e.g. urlencoded()) before csrf() so form submissions are validated against their token.

Use csrfSync for the sync fast path when no async middleware is in the chain.

proc csrfConstantTimeEqual(a, b: string): bool {.noSideEffect, ...raises: [],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Constant-time string comparison to prevent timing side-channels. Runs over the full length of the longer input (no early return) so the wall-clock cost does not depend on where a mismatch occurs or on the length difference; the length difference is folded into the diff. Both sides are normalized to lowercase for case-insensitive hex compare. 
proc csrfGenerateToken(): string {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Generates a 40-character lowercase hex token (20 random bytes). Not marked noSideEffect: it reads entropy via sysrand.urandom.
